## Release candidate scope

v2.0.0-rc.2 is a prerelease for evaluation, not a stable production baseline.
It follows v2.0.0-rc.1 and retains the current support policy: one Controller,
one database and one dedicated Relay, without HA. PostgreSQL 18.x and MySQL
8.4 LTS are the supported database engines. See the
[support policy](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.2/docs/reference/support-policy.md).

### Changes since RC.1

- Agents with ocserv below 1.4.2 no longer advertise session terminate; the
  privileged adapter also rejects that unsupported operation. Disconnect
  remains a separate operation.
- The Controller records acknowledged synchronous revocation updates and
  connection closes against the exact queued intent. ConfigPlan now accepts
  ocserv 1.5.0, matching the Agent adapter's existing admission.
- Validation adds protected-token enrollment, terminal revocation, real
  ocserv 1.5.0 session termination, Agent removal followed by Controller
  Offline, independent hosted-VM enrollment and bounded native platform checks.
  These checks do not expand the production support boundary.

### Breaking changes and upgrade notes

No additional breaking contract is introduced relative to RC.1. The v2.0.0
database transition still uses epoch 2: PostgreSQL revision 0 and MySQL
revision 1. The only supported prior database checkpoint is
`v1.2.0@169102557cd610847c9f6ac2083336cdcf82c483` (epoch 1 / revision 0).
Older databases must reach that checkpoint first. Upgrades are forward-only;
arbitrary historical upgrades and automatic database downgrades are unsupported.
Keep a verified backup and existing audit keys. Normal production Controller
startup requires `OCSERV_CONTROLLER_ENDPOINT_ID`. See the
[database migration contract](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.2/docs/development/control-plane.md#current-sql-artifacts-and-bounded-upgrades).

### Security and known limitations

- HTTP `503` with title `Revocation committed` means database revocation
  committed while transport synchronization remains uncertain. The synchronous
  success fix does not resolve lost RPC acknowledgements: when ownership has
  ended, convergence may remain pending/unknown. There is no guaranteed
  automatic recovery interval. Preserve the intent and evidence; do not blindly
  replay, bypass fences or edit convergence records. Follow
  [incident recovery](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.2/docs/operations/incident-recovery.md#revocation-committed-with-synchronization-pending).
- Full Business E2E has been validated on Ubuntu amd64. Ubuntu ARM64 and
  Debian 13 amd64/ARM64 have bounded native package/runtime/adapter evidence.
  Ubuntu ARM64 Controller E2E and Debian systemd/Controller E2E remain unverified.
  Hosted Cross-VM Enrollment does not certify Cross-VM Production, which still
  depends on external network authorization. See
  [validation scope](https://github.com/GentleKingson/ocservia/blob/v2.0.0-rc.2/docs/development/release-checks.md).
- The three exact `mysql_backup` image-scan exemptions remain subject to their
  existing 2026-10-26 review date, installed versions and pinned base digest.
  They cover reviewed Oracle Linux FIPS-channel mismatches, not other findings;
  new fixable High/Critical findings still block publication.
